additions.reason: The central concept of the entire Torah is צָרָה (distress/trouble/narrowness). The verse 'בַּצָּר הִרְחַבְתָּ לִּי' is interpreted to mean that God grants expansion WITHIN the distress itself — 'בְּהַצָּרָה בְּעַצְמָהּ.' The צרה is not merely the context but the very location of the הרחבה. The teaching establishes a paradoxical equivalence: the distress is simultaneously the narrowing AND the place of expansion. צרה is neutral in polarity — it is an experience that appears in both its negative aspect (constriction, suffering) and its positive aspect (the hidden container of divine expansion). This node should be encoded as a bechina partner of הרחבה for Torah #195, as the teaching's essential claim is that these two seemingly opposite states are co-present aspects of a single divine reality.
additions.source_quote: אֲפִלּוּ בְּהַצָּרָה בְּעַצְמָהּ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַרְחִיב לָנוּ

additions.reason: הַרְחָבָה (expansion, relief, breadth) is the counter-concept to צרה and the content of God's gift within distress. The text states: 'נָתַתָּ לִי הַרְחָבָה בְּתוֹכָהּ' — You gave me expansion WITHIN it (the distress). This is the positive pole of Torah #195's single conceptual pair. The teaching's entire argument is that the expansion is not merely future (a hoped-for salvation) but present — 'מִלְּבַד מַה שֶּׁאָנוּ מְצַפִּים שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ בְּקָרוֹב' (besides what we await). The הרחבה-within-צרה IS the bechina being established here. Polarity is good: expansion is the divine gift, the expression of God's kindness actively operating inside the narrowness.

חַסְדֵּי ה' (the kindnesses of God) is the perceptual lens through which the teaching operates. The text says: 'כִּי אִם יִסְתַּכֵּל הָאָדָם עַל חַסְדֵּי ה', יִרְאֶה שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ בְּעֵת שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵצֵר לוֹ, גַּם בְּהַצָּרָה בְּעַצְמָהּ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַרְחִיב לוֹ וּמַגְדִּיל חַסְדּוֹ עִמּוֹ.' Looking at God's kindnesses IS what reveals the הרחבה within the צרה. The act of looking (הסתכלות) at חסדי ה' is the epistemic entry point — it IS the perception of the expansion. In Rebbe Nachman's framework, חסד (lovingkindness) is a consistent bechina of divine expansion and outpouring. Here specifically, חסדי ה' is the name for what is experienced as הרחבה within the distress — God's kindness enlarges ('מַגְדִּיל חַסְדּוֹ') even at the moment of constriction. This makes חסדי ה' a bechina of הרחבה: they are two expressions of the same divine generosity operating within the צרה. Polarity: good.
additions.source_quote: אִם יִסְתַּכֵּל הָאָדָם עַל חַסְדֵּי ה', יִרְאֶה שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ בְּעֵת שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵצֵר לוֹ, גַּם בְּהַצָּרָה בְּעַצְמָהּ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַרְחִיב לוֹ

concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.description: Distress/narrowness — the primary subject of the Torah. The text repeatedly uses 'בְּהַצָּרָה בְּעַצְמָהּ' (within the distress itself) and 'הַצָּרוֹת' (the troubles). The Rebbe interprets the biblical 'בַּצָּר' (in narrowness) as teaching that the expansion occurs precisely INSIDE the distress — making צרה and הרחבה conceptual partners in a bechina relationship.
Expansion/relief — the divine gift given within the distress. 'נָתַתָּ לִי הַרְחָבָה בְּתוֹכָהּ' (You gave me expansion within it). The core positive concept of this Torah.

God's kindnesses — the lens of perception that reveals the expansion. The Rebbe says: if one looks at חסדי ה', one sees the הרחבה within the צרה. The text also says God 'מַגְדִּיל חַסְדּוֹ' (enlarges His kindness) — חסד/kindness IS the expansion within the distress.

Looking/contemplation — 'יִסְתַּכֵּל הָאָדָם' (a person should look/contemplate). The act of directed looking at חסדי ה' is the mechanism by which the hidden expansion within distress is perceived. This is eitza (contemplation produces perception), not bechina, so it does not qualify as a bechina addition.

analysis_notes.note_on_bechina_identification: Torah #195 uses no explicit bechina formula. The phrases 'הַיְנוּ' appear as interpretive glosses ('that is to say') rather than conceptual equations. The bechina insight is implicit in the teaching's paradox: the narrowness (צרה) IS the place of expansion (הרחבה) — they are not sequential (distress then relief) but simultaneous (expansion within the distress). This co-presence structure is the hallmark of bechina (parallel aspects of one reality) rather than eitza (one producing the other). The three proposed additions — צרה, הרחבה, and חסדי ה' — would form a single package of 3 nodes with 2 edges: (1) הרחבה ↔ צרה [expansion is the nature of the distress itself] and (2) חסדי ה' ↔ הרחבה [God's kindness IS the expansion within the distress].
analysis_notes.note_on_completeness: Torah #195 is among the shortest Torahs in Likutay Moharan Vol. 1 — just 3 lines of text. Its conceptual content is intentionally minimal: one verse, one paradox, one teaching. The three concepts above exhaust all bechina-eligible content in the source text. No additional bechina relationships exist to be encoded.
